title: Releasing the Past
coreMove: The past loosens when you feel what was stored, carry forward the lesson, and rebuild safety in the same life area where fear first taught defense.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers waiting for one perfect realization
exampleSpecs.stakes: A breakthrough fantasy can leave old behavior unchanged.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Ryan Holiday's 2016 epiphany warning to turn insight into repeated action.

exampleSpecs.audience: nurses distinguishing danger from present cues
exampleSpecs.stakes: A neutral tone could be misread as defiance if the body alarm is ignored.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Bremner's traumatic-stress systems to treat hypervigilance as protective neurobiology.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A promotion may soothe status fear without repairing relational safety.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Maslow's hierarchy to separate real safety from symbolic substitutes.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Avoidance can let one frightening cue occupy more of life.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show controlled exposure restoring a sense of competence.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers postponing life until they feel healed enough
exampleSpecs.stakes: Perfectionism can disguise itself as emotional readiness.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show healing beginning with the current self rather than a flawless imagined self.

exampleSpecs.audience: high achievers who use status to cover attachment fear
exampleSpecs.stakes: A symbolic win can fail to repair the domain where the wound formed.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Maslow's hierarchy to match the repair to the original safety rupture.
